// hello

Hello surfers, welcome to my personal page. I'm an engineering and science student at BITS Pilani, reading Electronics & Communication alongside Mathematics. I like open problems — the kind that don't have a single right answer.

My interests run broad: electronics, silicon, energy management, optimisation, aviation, music, football and cricket.

// 01 about

In my own words

I am currently interning at NuCurrent, where I work on GenA — their in-house applied-AI EDA platform that simulates circuit, thermal and EMI interactions to make wireless power antenna design dramatically faster — alongside hands-on hardware and firmware testing.

Before this, at Allegro MicroSystems, I spent a summer deep in analog design, running devices through Cadence Virtuoso and watching the same transistor behave differently across temperature, voltage and process corners. That attention to detail carried into my work as a Samsung ISWDP Fellow, where I trained on Sentaurus TCAD for semiconductor process simulation through a programme run with IISc Bangalore and Synopsys.

Know moreShow less

Alongside this industry experience, I've pursued research at BITS Pilani centred on modelling systems under uncertainty and optimising them within real-world constraints, with a recurring focus on sustainability and green energy. With Dr. Sumanta Pasari, I modelled the stochastic behaviour of wind and solar generation data, benchmarked distributional estimators, and applied that to a particle swarm optimisation model for energy trading in agrivoltaic systems under grid and tariff constraints.

With Dr. Rahul Singhal, I evaluated hardware implementations of the BB84, B92 and E91 quantum key distribution protocols, analysing trade-offs across source preparation, basis selection and detection schemes to propose a minimum-cost architecture for practical deployment. Different domains, but a shared thread: translating physical and statistical constraints into models that hold up in the real world.

What ties all of this together isn't a single specialisation but a willingness to move across domains — from transistor-level analog design to semiconductor process simulation, from energy systems modelling to quantum communication hardware, and now to antenna design and firmware at NuCurrent. This range doesn't dilute focus so much as sharpen it: each domain brings a different constraint to the table, and figuring out how to work within it is what I find genuinely interesting.

// 02 interests

My Interests

Eight domains, one habit: build a model of how something behaves, then go looking for where it stops being true.

Semiconductor Devices

What the transistor is actually doing underneath the model card.

Analog IC Design

Transistor-level circuits, where the answer is a waveform rather than a bit.

RTL & Digital Design

Describing a machine in SystemVerilog and watching it turn into cells.

Verification & Validation

Treating a design as wrong until a testbench and a coverage number say otherwise.

Applied Machine Learning

Models that have to earn their place against a simpler baseline.

Optimization Algorithms

Swarms, gradients and constraints pointed at objectives that pay for themselves.

Statistical Modelling

Fitting distributions to messy measured data, then testing how well the fit holds.

Sustainable Energy Management

Solar, wind, tariffs and storage — the economics on top of the physics.

// 04 projects

What I've built

Two on silicon, two on the mathematics underneath energy systems. Each opens up if you want the detail.

Sep 2026 — ongoing

RV32I core, RTL to sky130 with scan-based DFT

SystemVerilog · cocotb · Yosys · sky130 · Python
Independent project

A five-stage pipelined RISC-V core taken from RTL through synthesis to a sky130 layout, then attacked with a scan chain, a fault simulator and an ATPG engine written from scratch.

5,986standard cells
0.08mm² die area
15.8kfaults targeted
514test patterns
Stuck-at fault coverage0.00%
Know moreShow less
  • Five-stage pipelined RV32I core with forwarding, load-use stall and branch flush, beside a lint-clean single-cycle reference core.
  • A cocotb suite backed by Python reference models, 13 directed programs assembled by an RV32I assembler I wrote, and 10 hazard tests.
  • Synthesis to sky130 surfaced two RTL patterns that both lint and simulation had signed off on.
  • Scan insertion, bit-parallel stuck-at fault simulation and two-phase ATPG — random fill, then PODEM — written from scratch.
Source on GitHub
Aug — Dec 2025

QKD protocols on photonic devices

Photonics · optical fibre · systems costing
Supervised by Dr. Rahul Singhal, BITS Pilani

Evaluated hardware architectures for BB84, B92 and E91 quantum key distribution over optical fibre, then proposed a minimum-cost build that survives real components.

Know moreShow less
  • Evaluated hardware architectures for the BB84, B92 and E91 protocols in optical fibre systems.
  • Compared trade-offs across source preparation, basis selection and detection, each with a cost attached rather than treated as ideal.
  • Proposed a minimum-cost BB84 implementation optimised for practical deployment rather than ideal-component performance.
Jan — Jul 2025

Demand-side energy management for agrophotovoltaic systems

Python · particle swarm optimisation · real tariff data
Supervised by Dr. Sumanta Pasari, BITS Pilani

A particle swarm optimiser that maximises energy-trading revenue for agrivoltaic prosumers under real grid and tariff constraints.

Know moreShow less
  • Built a particle swarm optimiser for agrivoltaic prosumers under grid and tariff constraints, driven by real-world data rather than synthetic profiles.
  • Maximised energy-trading revenue across the dispatch schedule, with the constraint set doing the work a penalty term usually fudges.
  • Evaluated how the model performs and scales for actual deployment, not only on the training window.
Source on GitHub
Jan — Jul 2024

Statistical distributions for energy data analysis

Python · estimation theory · goodness-of-fit testing
Supervised by Dr. Sumanta Pasari, BITS Pilani

Fitted exponential-family distributions to solar and wind data, then benchmarked three estimators against each other to see which survived the tails.

Know moreShow less
  • Modelled solar and wind datasets with exponential-family distributions to capture their stochastic behaviour rather than smoothing it away.
  • Benchmarked method of moments, maximum likelihood and L-moments estimators on the same data using statistical fit metrics.
  • Drew out what the fits imply for uncertainty modelling and grid-level forecasting — the groundwork the optimiser stands on.
